name: Build a prototype
description: Builds one prototype ticket from the scratch directory: the smallest throwaway code that tries out its approach, on its own branch (run it in a worktree that isn't merged back), then writes <ticket>_REPORT.md saying what happened and how to try it. A person approves the prototype afterwards, in the flow that ran it.

parameters.label: Ticket
parameters.description: The prototype's id: its file name in the scratch directory without .md, e.g. prototype-003-streaming-parser.

parameters.label: The document it serves
parameters.description: The file in the scratch directory the spike settles a question for, e.g. SPECS.md (the draft specs) or OPTIONS.md (architecture options).

steps.name: Build the prototype
steps.prompt:
Build prototype {{params.ticket}} of {{ticket.title}}.

Read the prototype ticket, {{scratch.path}}/{{params.ticket}}.md, and the draft it serves, {{scratch.path}}/{{params.brief}}.

Build the smallest thing that answers its question: throwaway code is fine, and it won't be merged, but it must actually run so a person can try it. Run it, and any quick check or measurement the ticket asks for. Don't commit, and don't switch branches: afl keeps your work on its own branch.

Report what you built, file by file, how to run it, and what happened when you did.

steps.name: Write the report
steps.prompt:
Write the report for prototype {{params.ticket}} ({{scratch.path}}/{{params.ticket}}.md). Do not change any files.

What the build did:
{{steps.build.output}}

Look at the change (git status, git diff HEAD) and the branch (git branch --show-current) if you need to. Reply with the report, in markdown, and nothing else:

# Report: {{params.ticket}}
## Question
## What was built
(file by file)
## How to try it
(the branch, and the commands to run)
## What happened
## Answer
(what the prototype shows, and how sure you are)
## What it means for {{params.brief}}
